title: Resilience Gatekeeper: probe calibration, regional failover choreography, and controlled shedding playbook
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Background: Recent incidents showed that simple binary readiness checks lead to brittle autoscaler behavior during partial region degradation. We need an operational pattern that harmonizes probe semantics across services, provides a single "Resilience Gatekeeper" layer for cross-region decisions, and guarantees SLO preservation through graceful, observable shedding and circuit-breaker choreography.

Goal: Define and implement a playbook + small runtime shim that: 1) standardizes probe weights and health envelopes across critical services; 2) exposes a Gatekeeper API that fuses local probe signals into a region-level health score; 3) integrates with autoscaler and traffic-router for token-weighted shedding and staged failover to preserve p99 latency SLOs; 4) provides canary/chaos test harness and dashboards for verification.

Scope: prototype Gatekeeper shim + per-service probe adapters (runtime config only, no core runtime changes), autoscaler admission hook for de-rated scale decisions, Grafana dashboards and alerts, documentation and runbook. Exclude: rewriting model-serving kernels or GPU allocation logic.

Trade-offs/Constraints:
- Adding a Gatekeeper introduces an extra decision path; we must keep it lightweight and fail-open to avoid creating a single point of failure.
- Conservative probe smoothing reduces noise but increases time-to-detect real failures; we will tune via synthetic traffic and SLO-aware regression tests.
- Staged shedding trades availability for latency: for some enterprise customers we will prefer regional routing rather than aggressive shedding (config overrides).

Plan overview:
1) Probe harmonization RFC (this ticket references the RFC doc) -> standardize probe categories (soft-warning, hard-readiness, capacity-signal) and associated weights.
2) Build Gatekeeper shim (Go): ingest local probes, apply EWMA + min-healthy-window, output region health score + reason codes. Expose REST + Prometheus metrics.
3) Autoscaler integration: admission controller consults Gatekeeper to derate scale decisions (delay scale-to-zero, prefer vertical/higher-priority token routing).
4) Traffic-router integration: add staged circuit-breaker policies (soft-drop, token-weighted shedding, then regional drain) with explicit fallback models.
5) Verification: runbook, synthetic load campaign across 3 regions, chaos scenarios (node loss, network partitions), and SLO regression checks.

Acceptance criteria, monitoring, and rollback conditions are enumerated below.
acceptance_criteria: Gatekeeper service deployed in staging per region and emitting prometheus metrics for region_health_score{service,region} and probe_reason_codes
Default probe adapter implemented for two critical services (runtime-api, router) and using standardized weight set
Autoscaler admission controller uses gatekeeper health score to prevent scale-downs that would violate p99 latency SLO in >90% of simulated degradations
Traffic-router can perform token-weighted shedding with documented config and observable traffic-shift metrics; synthetic tests show p99 preserved within target under degraded region
Dashboard with burn-rate, region_health_score, shed_rate, and autoscale_decision_count created and alerted; alert runbook includes automatic rollback to fail-open mode
Canary in prod (1 region, low traffic) completed with no customer-facing errors and clear metric baselines
Runbook for manual intervention and postmortem checklist published in Confluence
comments: 2025-02-18 Maya Thompson: Created ticket after incident review. Goal to stabilize autoscaler handoffs during regional flapping and to provide an operational gatekeeper that reduces oscillation.
2025-02-21 Alejandro Ruiz: Switched status to In Progress. Started probe category RFC draft and simple EWMA prototype; initial tests show reduced flip-flop on 5s probe bursts.

2025-02-24 Engineering review (Kaya Singh): Feedback - prefer percentiles over mean for probe smoothing, add min-healthy-window to avoid short blips. Also requested explicit reason codes for shedding decisions.
2025-02-26 Alejandro Ruiz: PR opened for gatekeeper shim (see links). Implemented metrics and basic rest endpoint. Performance microbenchmark: added <2ms p99 CPU overhead on a small t3-like instance.

2025-03-01 QA (Rohit Patel): Ran synthetic degradation tests against staging; observed that aggressive EWMA settings delayed failover more than acceptable; proposed tuning: alpha=0.25, min_window=30s.
2025-03-02 Product (Jun Park): Approved canary plan for low-traffic region; asked for explicit enterprise opt-out toggle (will be config flag per customer-account).
2025-03-02 Alejandro Ruiz: Next steps - finalize RFC, run broader chaos campaign, tune gatekeeper parameters, open autoscaler integration PR, schedule canary during maintenance window.
